old_value: The represented mechanic changes defense, not outgoing TDD.
new_value: Every declared family on this item is a defence: the represented mechanic changes durability, not outgoing TDD.

evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.isolation_note: Only data/ and docs/math-foundations.md were read. src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, git history, the diff and the plan were never opened.

leaf_nature: This leaf is a prose justification string, not a numeric quantity. It cannot be arrived at by arithmetic; it is checked by (a) whether the causal claim it makes is true of the cached game text, and (b) whether the quantified premise it adds is consistent with the cached declarations.

step_1_define_TDD.claim: TDD in this codebase = total damage dealt by the main participant, the optimizer objective.
step_1_define_TDD.source: docs/math-foundations.md sec. 3.1: "f(S) = the coupled participant-timeline score: deterministic total damage dealt by the main participant before its own death, summed over the fight window, with an infinitesimal effective-health tiebreak (score + EHP*1e-9)".
step_1_define_TDD.consequence: Effective health / durability enters only as an infinitesimal 1e-9 tiebreak, never as damage. So a purely defensive mechanic contributes 0 to TDD by construction — the shared clause of BOTH strings is true whenever the mechanic is defensive.

step_2_family_taxonomy.claim: The cache declares an effect 'family' per atom; the vocabulary contains no 'defence' family, so 'defence' is a coverage-layer classification over the declared families, not a literal cache label.
sources: data/atoms/classification-report.json -> vocab.families = [crowd-control-mobility, damage, heal-shield, interaction, stack-transform-summon-resource, vision-economy]

data/item-atoms/*.json -> per-item atoms, each with a 'family' field; item family census over 324 items = {stats: 586, damage: 348, heal-shield: 266, stack-transform-summon-resource: 248, vision-economy: 190, crowd-control-mobility: 137}
step_2_family_taxonomy.consequence: The premise 'every declared family on this item is a defence' is a statement about the item's declared non-stat effect families all being durability-side (heal-shield / defensive stats). That premise is checkable per item against data/item-atoms/.

step_3_discriminating_test.method: Enumerate the items whose declared effect (non-stat) families are entirely durability-side, and the near-miss items that would fail such a premise. If the premise is a real discriminator, the items it admits must genuinely have no outgoing-damage mechanic, and the items that superficially look defensive but do change outgoing damage must be rejected by it.
rejected_by_premise (a 'damage' family i: Abyssal Mask (8020): atoms = stats.health, stats.magic-resistance, stats.ability-haste, damage.magic|Unmake. Cached wiki text: "Enemy champions within 700 units of you become cursed, causing them to receive 12% increased magic damage from all sources." -> this item's mechanic DOES raise outgoing TDD. Old string ('changes defense, not outgoing TDD') would be FALSE here; the new string's premise blocks it.
Zhonya's Hourglass (3157): atoms include crowd-control-mobility.stasis and damage.resistance-mitigation (Time Stop).
Seraph's Embrace (3040): atoms include stack-transform-summon-resource.mana (Awe converts mana to AP -> outgoing damage).
Thornmail (3075), Sunfire Aegis (3068), Randuin's Omen (3143), Frozen Heart (3110), Force of Nature (4401): all declare a 'damage' family.
step_3_discriminating_test.verdict_of_test: The added premise is a real, cache-checkable guard that separates genuinely durability-only mechanics from defensive-looking items that do move outgoing damage (Abyssal Mask being the sharpest case). The old string asserted the conclusion with no stated basis; the new string states the basis and is therefore self-certifying against data/item-atoms/.

step_4_terminology.claim: 'durability' is the League's own umbrella term for health/resistances/shields; there is no single 'defense' stat in the game.
sources: data/wiki/article-index.json -> article "Durability" (pageid 961552) exists; "Armor" (3258) and "Magic resistance" (3259) are separate articles; there is no "Defense" stat article (only historical mastery-tree pages: "Defense Mastery Tree (2011..2014)").
step_4_terminology.consequence: 'changes durability' is the more accurate wording than 'changes defense' for a mechanic like a spell shield, which alters neither armor nor MR but does alter durability.

step_5_applied_to_the_scenario_item.note: The scenario definition for syndra_custom_order_39 lives outside the permitted evidence tree (it is not in data/ — grep for 'custom_order' and 'item_coverage' over data/ + docs/math-foundations.md returns nothing but data/worklists/e9-bis-b-task.md, which describes the item-coverage mechanism but names no Syndra scenario). The item at item_coverage[0] therefore cannot be named from the export.
step_5_applied_to_the_scenario_item.reasoning_without_the_name: The leaf is a utility_outcomes entry, i.e. an item the engine already routed to non-damage outcomes. For every item admitted by the stated premise the conclusion holds; for a Syndra (AP) build the admitted candidates are Banshee's Veil / Verdant Barrier (Annul) and Spirit Visage — all purely durability-side. Cached wiki text for Annul: "Grants a spell shield that blocks the next hostile ability (40 second cooldown, timer restarts upon taking damage from champions)." — no term of this effect enters any damage formula, so its TDD contribution is exactly 0 and its EHP contribution enters only via the 1e-9 tiebreak.
step_5_applied_to_the_scenario_item.falsification_test_left_open: If item_coverage[0] were Abyssal Mask (8020), BOTH strings would be wrong (Unmake raises outgoing magic damage by 12%). The cache rejects Abyssal Mask under the new string's own premise (it declares family 'damage'), so the new string cannot be emitted for it consistently; the old string had no such guard. That asymmetry is why the new value is the safer and more correct of the two.

caveat_flagged.issue: If the coverage layer derives 'declared family' from data/item-atoms/, the premise is only as complete as those declarations, and two items in the cache under-declare their damage.
instances: Eclipse (6692): item-atoms declare only heal-shield.shield|Ever Rising Moon, but items.json passive text says the second stack "deals bonus physical damage".

Divine Sunderer (446632): item-atoms declare only heal-shield.heal / heal-shield.vamp|Spellblade, but items.json passive text says the empowered attack "deals 180% base AD (+ 6%/4% of target's maximum health) as bonus physical damage on-hit".
caveat_flagged.impact_on_this_leaf: None — neither item is a plausible AP-mage utility entry, and both are AD legendaries. But the same reason string would be emitted incorrectly for them if the guard reads item-atom families alone. Recorded as an aside, not as a defect of this leaf.

conclusion: Both strings share the same causal claim, which is true for any durability-only mechanic given the TDD definition in docs/math-foundations.md. The new string additionally states the cache-checkable premise that licenses that claim, uses the game's own umbrella term ('durability') in place of a stat that does not exist ('defense'), and — decisively — its premise is exactly the guard that excludes defensive-looking items whose declared families include 'damage' and which therefore DO change outgoing TDD (Abyssal Mask's Unmake, +12% magic damage taken). Nothing in the cached data falsifies the new string; the old string is a weaker, unsourced form of the same assertion.
